title: Hybrid multimodel service-coupling microbenchmark for continuous-batching + queue dynamics
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Run a focused microbenchmark that quantifies how continuous batching interacts with request queueing under heterogeneous traffic mixes (short chat-like requests, long generation sessions, and high-embedding bursts) and produce statistically robust token/sec and tail-latency p95/p99 surfaces.

Motivation: Existing synthetic probes cover isolated arrival shapes; we need repeatable, multimodel service-level tests that capture coupling effects between batch filling, KV cache effectiveness, and queue occupancy when multiple model sizes/quantization profiles are served on a shared GPU pool. This will inform autoscaling, batching windows, and routing fallback policies.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Produce end-to-end test harness that can run stable 30m to 3h experiments across configurable mixes and concurrency targets.
- Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 generation latency, queue-occupancy histogram, batch size distribution, KV cache hit-rate, and per-request token cost.
- Detect regressions vs baseline using both non-parametric (bootstrap CI on medians/p95) and control chart (EWMA) approaches; auto-pass/fail decision with configurable thresholds.
- Visualize results in console dashboard (time-series + heatmap) and persist raw traces to S3 for deeper analysis.
- Benchmark variability: less than 5% coefficient of variation for primary metric (tokens/sec) in steady-state runs >=30m for the standard mix.

Test matrix (initial):
- Workload mixes: {70% short-chat (avg 50 tokens), 20% long-gen (avg 1024 tokens), 10% embeddings bursts (avg 1024), with an alternate balanced mix 40/40/20}.
- Model set: small language model (7B quantized), medium (13B 4-bit), and large (34B float16) with routing weights configurable.
- Concurrency surface: 10, 50, 150, 400 concurrent sessions (session semantics: maintain KV across turns for long-gen).
- Batching configs: continuous-batching (0 ms window), dynamic-window (10–100 ms), and fixed-window (20 ms).
- Backpressure policies: drop/queue-with-circuit-breaker/fanout-to-fallback-model.

Harness architecture:
- Traffic generator: multi-process Go tool that replays arrival traces and synthesizes new traces via a configurable mixture model; supports sticky sessions to emulate KV cache reuse.
- Collector: lightweight agent that tags and emits per-request telemetry (timestamps for queue entry/exit, batch id, batch size, model variant, tokens emitted) to a telemetry stream (Kafka).
- Analysis: batch postprocessing jobs (Spark or Flink) compute per-experiment summaries and bootstrap CIs. A regression-checker microservice compares new experiment summaries to baselines and posts results to the dashboard.

Measurement methodology:
- Tokens/sec = sum(tokens_emitted)/active_processing_seconds (exclude time while no instances running).
- Latency percentiles computed from generation-start to generation-end (exclude network driver overhead where measurable).
- Queue occupancy: sampled every 50 ms and aggregated to histogram.
- Baseline determination: median of 5 stable runs for the default mix on the same infra flavor.

Regression detection:
- Primary check: bootstrap 95% CI on tokens/sec and p95 latency; fail if new median is outside baseline median ± delta or if bootstrap CIs do not overlap, using delta = 5% for tokens/sec and delta = +10% for p95 latency in initial tuning.
- Secondary check: EWMA on tokens/sec with lambda=0.2 to catch gradual drifts; alert if drift exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive windows.
- Flakiness mitigation: require two consecutive experiments failing to mark a regression unless failure magnitude > 20% tokens/sec or >30% p95 latency.

Deliverables:
- Bench harness repo with README and experiment recipes (short/default/peak).
- Console dashboard panel with heatmap of p95 across mixes x concurrency and a tokens/sec surface plot.
- Regression checker service + alerting hook to #bench-regressions Slack.
- Design doc describing statistical tests and recommended threshold values.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Running long multimodel experiments is expensive; we will use smaller cluster sizes for early iterations and only run full-sweep on dedicated CI capacity.
- Accurate isolation of driver vs runtime latency requires kernel-level instrumentation which may be noisy on shared infra; we will add a control calibration run that measures driver overhead separately.

Notes / Links:
- Initial design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Hybrid+Multimodel+Microbenchmark (draft)
- Proto traffic generator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-traffic-gen/pull/58
- Related experiments: ENG-70192 (tail-aware throughput surface), ENG-84211 (hybrid-load-curve synthesis)

Next steps:
1) Finish instrumentation for batch-id propagation (PR referenced below).
2) Wire telemetry to Kafka topic bench.telemetry.v2 and verify schema.
3) Run three 30m baseline runs for the standard mix on staging-gpu-2 and collect artifacts.
4) Draft console dashboard tiles and share with PM/Design for review.
